plan_title: Archer Daniels Midland Company, ADM Decatur Corn Processing, Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan CCS#2
ama_definition: Set equal to the MMA: the Area of Review from the Class VI permit plus a half-mile buffer, held constant through injection and the 10-year post-injection period (p12, p14).
mma_definition: The permit Area of Review plus a half-mile buffer, i.e. the stabilized plume (modeled to stabilize 4 years after injection, 6.5 million t total from CCS#1 and CCS#2) plus a half mile, radius about 8,260 ft (p12, p14).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Only surface components (the ~5,000 ft pipeline and wellhead) are rated 'possible'; injection/monitoring wells are 'highly improbable', faults/fractures and confining-zone limitations 'highly improbable to nearly impossible', and abandoned wells 'almost impossible' because none penetrate the Eau Claire seal (p15-18).
baseline_summary: Pre-injection baselines: groundwater quality/geochemistry (completed 08/09/2015, accepted range set statistically with ProUCL at 95% limits), injection-well pulsed neutron and temperature logs (9/30/2015) and shut-in DTS profile (12/31/2016), MIT logs and pressure tests on CCS#2 and VW#2 (2012-2015), RST logs in CCS#1, CCS#2, VW#1, VW#2 (2014-2016), 3D seismic and VSP surveys (2011, 2015), and pre-injection seismicity. Injection and annulus pressures are explicitly not baseline parameters (p20, p29-32).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with mass balance (CO2 injected by Coriolis meter minus surface leakage and equipment/vented emissions, RR-4/6, RR-10, RR-12); records kept per permit Section N in electronic form at Decatur. Through the incorporated Class VI permit, monitoring results go to EPA's UIC program in semiannual reports, with 24-hour reporting of noncompliance, MIT reports within 30 days and 10-year record retention; seismic events above thresholds reported to the UIC Director and ISGS within 24 hours. No commitment to publish monitoring data (p24, p32-34, p55-58, p65-66).

rows.detail: Coriolis mass flow meter (FE006) on the injection line measures CO2 injected; CO2 stream sampled quarterly after the last compression stage and analyzed by a third-party lab; annual mass from quarterly flow times quarterly concentration.
rows.location: Compression facility / injection line to CCS#2
rows.evidence_quote: Flow will be monitored with a Coriolis mass flowmeter at the compression facility.

rows.detail: Wellhead and downhole (at packer) pressure and temperature recorded continuously (sampled every 5 s, recorded every 5 min) by a distributed control system that alarms and shuts down outside normal ranges; surface pressure capped at 2,284 psig.
rows.location: CCS#2 wellhead and tubing at packer
rows.trigger_or_response: Anomalous readings trigger investigation; automatic alarm/shut-off; loss of integrity or equipment failure: shut in, notify UIC Director within 24 hours.
rows.evidence_quote: Pressure and temperature will be continuously monitored during injection operations, at the surface (wellhead), at the injection zone, and in the well annulus.

rows.detail: Continuous annulus pressure gauge with a pressurized annulus head tank (about 425-525 psi) and minimum 100 psi differential across the packer; average annulus pressure and tank fluid level recorded daily, fluid added or removed logged.
rows.trigger_or_response: Significant annulus pressure changes investigated under the emergency plan; QASP action limit is more than 3% pressure loss over one hour.
rows.evidence_quote: During the injection timeframe of the project, the casing-tubing pressure will be monitored and recorded in real time.

rows.detail: Annual external MIT on CCS#2 by temperature log (DTS or wireline), noise log or oxygen activation log; DTS gives real-time integrity surveillance; pressure fall-off tests mid-injection and at end of injection (permit: at least every five years); annual alarm/shut-off test.
rows.location: CCS#2 injection well (baseline MIT also on VW#2)
rows.trigger_or_response: Failed MIT or loss of integrity: cease injection, determine any release, restore integrity and get Director approval before resuming.
rows.evidence_quote: MITs will be performed annually, up to 45 days before the anniversary date of authorization of injection each year

rows.detail: Downhole pressure/temperature gauges in the Mt. Simon: VW#2 (4 intervals) continuous, VW#1 continuous in years 1-3 only, CCS#1 and CCS#2 at the packer continuous; continued in post-injection (CCS#1/CCS#2 annual after year 3).
rows.trigger_or_response: Unexpected pressure change beyond three standard deviations, or above 90% of fracture pressure, triggers an unscheduled AoR reevaluation.
rows.evidence_quote: ADM will deploy pressure/temperature monitors and DTS to directly monitor the position of the pressure front.

rows.detail: Monthly visual inspection of the aboveground pipeline and wellhead for ice crystal formation from leaking CO2; the buried, fully welded pipeline segment is checked only by abnormal pressure drops during shut-ins.
rows.location: Pipeline from flow meter to CCS#2 wellhead
rows.trigger_or_response: Leak seen: photograph, map on P&ID, isolate pipeline or stop injection, estimate leak rate and mass.
rows.evidence_quote: Visual monitoring for these emissions will be performed monthly to detect fugitive emissions.

rows.detail: Permit allows soil gas monitoring only if the Director requires it; the 2011 permit application says soil gas monitoring is not proposed given the low risk.
rows.evidence_quote: soil gas monitoring is not proposed for this permit.

rows.detail: Four shallow Quaternary/Pennsylvanian wells (MVA10LG-MVA13LG) sampled quarterly in years 1-2, semiannually in years 3-5, annually post-injection; lowermost USDW (St. Peter) sampled annually at GM#2; metals, anions, dissolved CO2, TDS, alkalinity, field parameters, St. Peter d13C.
rows.location: 4 shallow wells on ADM property; GM#2 (St. Peter)
rows.trigger_or_response: Values outside baseline range: verify per QASP; confirmed: shut in, confirmation sampling, delineate and remediate USDW with UIC Director.
rows.evidence_quote: Shallow groundwater samples will be collected on a quarterly basis in years 1-2 of injection, semi-annual sampling for years 3-5 of injection

rows.detail: Ironton-Galesville (directly above the Eau Claire seal) fluid sampling at VW#2 annually (VW#1 years 1-3) with continuous pressure/temperature at VW#2 (VW#1 years 1-3); St. Peter pressure/temperature at GM#2; geochemical and isotopic (d13C DIC) indicators.
rows.trigger_or_response: Statistically significant difference from baseline above the confining zone triggers QASP verification and an unscheduled AoR reevaluation.
rows.evidence_quote: wells monitoring the deeper formations (St. Peter and Ironton/Galesville) are monitored for changes in geochemical and isotopic signatures

rows.detail: Pulsed neutron/RST saturation logs in VW#1, VW#2, CCS#1 and CCS#2 at baseline and years 2 and 4 of injection, then post-injection years 1, 3, 5, 7, 10; wireline temperature, noise or oxygen activation logs as MIT options; DTS temperature profiles.
rows.trigger_or_response: CO2 saturation increase into or above the confining zone triggers AoR reevaluation unless traced to well integrity.
rows.evidence_quote: pulse neutron logging / reservoir saturation testing in VW#1, VW#2, CCS#1, and CCS#2 every two years during the injection phase

rows.detail: ADM's own network of borehole and surface seismic stations detects events above M1.0 within about 8 miles/the AoR, continuously through post-injection; USGS national network and felt reports also used; compared with pre-injection seismicity.
rows.location: Multiple stations within the AoR, 8-mile radius of CCS#2
rows.trigger_or_response: Traffic-light plan: above M1.5 with felt report or above M2.0, notify UIC Director/ISGS in 24 hours; larger events reduce rate or shut in well.
rows.evidence_quote: ADM will maintain a network of seismic monitoring stations to detect natural or induced seismic events greater than magnitude 1.0

rows.detail: Time-lapse 3D surface seismic: baseline 2011 and 2015 surveys, reduced-scale repeat in 2021, another planned about 2030 (year 10 post-injection); VSP from GM#1 in 2013-2015 near CCS#1 already done.
rows.location: Northern part of plume area near CCS#2 (~2,000 acres; fold coverage ~650 acres)
rows.trigger_or_response: Seismic data showing a fault or fracture in or near the confining zone triggers an AoR reevaluation.
rows.evidence_quote: conducted in 2021, and another is planned for year 10 following the conclusion of injection operations (approximately 2030).

rows.detail: Permit requires surface air monitoring only if the Director asks; the 2011 permit application says surface air monitoring is not proposed.
rows.evidence_quote: surface air monitoring is not proposed for this permit.

rows.detail: Direct plume monitoring: fluid sampling of the Mt. Simon injection zone at VW#2 (3 intervals) annually and VW#1 in years 1-3, analyzed for metals, anions, dissolved CO2, d13C DIC and field parameters.
rows.trigger_or_response: Anomaly not explained by reservoir conditions or model uncertainty is treated as verified leakage.
rows.evidence_quote: The plume will be directly monitored via annual fluid sampling in the Mt. Simon using VW#2 and/or other nearby monitoring wells.

rows.detail: Corrosion coupons (pipeline, casing, tubing, wellhead, packer materials) in a flow-through loop at the start of the pipeline, weighed and measured quarterly.
rows.location: Flow-through loop at beginning of pipeline to wellhead
rows.evidence_quote: ADM will monitor corrosion using the corrosion coupon method

rows.detail: Area of Review reevaluation every five years with model history-matching against monitoring data; monitoring and operating data reviewed periodically (likely annually).
rows.trigger_or_response: Deviations from predicted plume or pressure front trigger an unscheduled AoR reevaluation and model recalibration.
rows.evidence_quote: ADM will reevaluate the above described AoR every five years during the injection and post-injection phases.

rows.detail: Leaks quantified only after detection: surface leaks and relief-valve releases estimated from operating conditions and duration; subsurface leaks by mass-balance estimate or a calibrated 'leaky' reservoir model, with statistical error estimate.
rows.location: Pipeline relief valves (TRV-001-003), annulus PSVs, wellhead, subsurface
rows.trigger_or_response: Subsurface leakage assumed to reach the surface unless modeling shows otherwise.
rows.evidence_quote: ADM will estimate the mass of CO2 emitted from relief valves or leakage points based on operating conditions at the time of the release

notes: Hand-coded in session (not by the API batch): the API declined to process this plan. The supplied text file is unreadable: the PDF's embedded fonts lack Unicode mappings, so nearly every page extracted as substitution-cipher garbage. To code it, the public PDF was re-downloaded from the plan_url in sources_national.json (SHA-256 matched the recorded hash) and the needed pages were OCR'd with tesseract; quotes come from that OCR and page numbers are PDF pages (same numbering as the text file). The MRV plan itself is only PDF pages 2-38 and relies on Reference 1 (the CCS#2 Class VI permit, p42-282: Attachment C Testing and Monitoring Plan p90-119, QASP p120-223, PISC plan p229-259, emergency plan p260-274) and Reference 2 (2011 permit application, p284-594); rows draw on these incorporated documents. Several QASP tables are rotated (p130-145) and were not read. Wells: the plan covers only CCS#2 (permit IL-115-6A-0001); CCS#1 (the IBDP well, separate permit IL-115-6A-0002) is not an injector under this plan but is used as a monitoring point (downhole P/T, DTS, RST logs). Commitments differ by well: DTS and annual MIT are described for CCS#2; Mt. Simon fluid sampling at VW#2 annually but VW#1 only years 1-3; Ironton-Galesville P/T continuous at VW#2 but VW#1 only years 1-3; VSP used GM#1 near CCS#1; St. Peter monitoring at GM#2; baseline MIT on CCS#2 and VW#2. Inconsistencies: minimum surface annulus pressure is 100 psi in the MRV plan (p29) but 400 psi in Attachment C (p94); the MRV calls the Pennsylvanian bedrock the lowermost USDW (p7) but later the St. Peter (p22); total injection given as 6 million t (p7) and 6.5 million t (p12); repeat 3D seismic is dated year 2 (2019) in Attachment C, est. 2020 in the PISC plan, and 2021 in the MRV plan. The MRV plan cites 'Section 5' for groundwater monitoring, which appears to mean Section 9.1.2.2. Reservoir-pressure baseline coded 'unclear' because the plan lists 'pressure front data' as baseline but names no pre-injection pressure measurement for it. Soil gas and surface air coded mentioned_only (only 'if required by the Director'; the application says neither is proposed).
